question: A closed Amperian path encloses four long conductors carrying currents $8\text{ A}$, $5\text{ A}$, $3\text{ A}$ and $4\text{ A}$. The first two currents are out of the plane of the path and the last two are into the plane. Taking outward current as positive, calculate $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l}$. Explain whether the value changes if the shape of the closed path is changed without changing the enclosed currents. Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}$.

options.A: $I_{\text{enc}}=8+5+3+4=20\,\text{A}$, so $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l=80\pi\times10^{-7}\,\text{T m}$; it changes with the path shape.
options.B: $I_{\text{enc}}=8-5-3-4=-4\,\text{A}$, so $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l=-16\pi\times10^{-7}\,\text{T m}$; it is zero only for circular paths.
options.C: Taking outward currents positive, $I_{\text{enc}}=8+5-3-4=6\,\text{A}$. Thus, $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l=\mu_0I_{\text{enc}}=24\pi\times10^{-7}\,\text{T m}$. It remains unchanged for any closed path enclosing the same net current.
options.D: $I_{\text{enc}}=8+5-3-4=6\,\text{A}$, so $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l=\dfrac{\mu_0I_{\text{enc}}}{2\pi}=12\times10^{-7}\,\text{T m}$; it changes if the path shape changes.
